c:get_zero_initialized_log_levels.why: rcl's zero-init idiom for a type we do not have; see `c:log_levels_*`. Same shape as `c:get_zero_initialized_init_options` in the init stage.

c:log_default_logger.why: the C logging surface, reachable from the umbrella header since issue 0795 was fixed (`nros.hpp` always included its C++ twin). ROS 2's counterpart is rcutils logging, which we decline as a whole -- see the log stage -- because it carries per-logger level maps, an installable output handler and a formatted-message buffer per thread. Ours emits through the platform sink the board installed. This is the entry point a C author must find FIRST: reaching for `printf` instead is fatal on Zephyr native_sim (issue 0589), which is why the umbrella omitting it was a hazard and not just a discoverability nit.

c:log_levels_*.why: rcl's `rcl_log_levels_t` is a heap-allocated growable array of (logger name, severity) pairs with an `rcl_allocator_t` member, populated from `--ros-args --log-level`; `init` / `fini` / `copy` / `shrink_to_size` are its memory lifecycle and nothing else. Constraints: no allocator and no argv (RFC-0045). Ours is a per-`Logger` `AtomicU8` threshold living inside the `'static Logger` itself (`nros_log::Logger::{level, set_level, is_enabled}`) reached through a bounded 32-entry intern table (`nros_log::MAX_LOGGERS`), so there is no separate collection to allocate, copy, shrink or free. The compile-time half of the same knob is the `max-level-*` Cargo features, checked by the `const fn severity_enabled_at_compile_time` the macros expand into. The one member of this family that is a CAPABILITY rather than memory management has its own row -- see `c:log_levels_add_logger_setting`.

c:log_levels_add_logger_setting.why:
rcl's "set THIS logger's level", and the one member of `rcl_log_levels_*` that is a capability rather than allocation bookkeeping. The SHAPE is declined with the rest of the family (`c:log_levels_*`): it takes an `rcl_log_levels_t *` — a heap-allocated growable array of (name, severity) pairs carrying an `rcl_allocator_t`, populated from `--ros-args --log-level` — and we have no allocator and no argv (RFC-0045). The CAPABILITY inside it is not declined and is no longer missing.

CORRECTION (2026-09-13). This row was a `gap` reading: "C and C++ have NO way to reach it: `<nros/log.h>` exposes only `nros_log_emit`, `nros_log_emit_fmt`, `nros_log_init` and `nros_log_default_logger`, and there is no `nros_logger_set_level` / `nros_logger_get_level` on the `nros_logger_t` handle." Every clause of that is now false. phase-417 W4.d shipped `nros_logger_set_level` / `nros_logger_get_level` / `nros_logger_is_enabled` beside `nros_log_get_logger` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/log.h`), and the C++ half landed as `cpp:Logger::set_level` on 2026-09-13. The row is re-verdicted rather than deleted because rcl's TYPE is still declined and a reader arriving from `rcl_log_levels_add_logger_setting` needs to be told where the capability went: `c:logger_set_level`, `c:logger_get_level`, `c:logger_is_enabled`.

The old row also recorded that `examples/native/c/logging/src/main.c`'s file comment claimed a threshold helper the file did not contain. That is the example's to fix and is not this row's subject; the accessor it described now exists.

c:logger_setting_t.why: the (name, severity) pair `rcl_log_levels_t` holds an array of. Ours is the `Logger` object itself -- name plus `AtomicU8` threshold, `const`-constructible as a `static`. See `c:log_levels_*`.

c:logger_t.why:
the C logging surface, reachable from the umbrella header since issue 0795 was fixed (`nros.hpp` always included its C++ twin). ROS 2's counterpart is rcutils logging. CORRECTION (2026-09-13): this row said we decline it as a whole "because it carries per-logger level maps, an installable output handler and a formatted-message buffer per thread" and that "ours emits through the platform sink the board installed". Two of those three shipped in phase-417 W4.d — a bounded per-logger level table (`nros_log_get_logger` + `nros_logger_set_level`) and an installable sink (`nros_log_add_sink`, which APPENDS to the board's rather than replacing it). The per-thread formatted-message buffer is still declined: `NROS_LOG_FMT_BUFFER_SIZE` is a 256-byte stack buffer at the call site, because a per-thread buffer needs an allocator or a thread-count bound and neither exists here. What the rest of this row argues — that there is no logger HANDLE type in rcutils to correlate against — is unaffected. This is the entry point a C author must find FIRST: reaching for `printf` instead is fatal on Zephyr native_sim (issue 0589), which is why the umbrella omitting it was a hazard and not just a discoverability nit.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. W2 F14, and the finding's wording NARROWED: rcutils has no logger HANDLE type at all — its API is `rcutils_log(location, severity, const char *name, format, ...)` — so the pointer a porting user most plausibly hands us is the logger NAME (`const char *`), and rclcpp's is an `rclcpp::Logger` object. Say "any pointer, including a logger name", not "an rcutils logger type".

THE FINDING: `typedef const void *nros_logger_t` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/log.h`) is the parameter type of ten functions (`nros_log_emit`, `nros_log_emit_fmt`, the two `_at` forms, `nros_log_default_logger`, `nros_log_get_logger`, `nros_logger_get_name`, `nros_logger_set_level`, `nros_logger_get_level`, `nros_logger_is_enabled`). In C every object pointer converts to `const void *` implicitly, with no diagnostic at any warning level, and the Rust side then does `&*(logger as *const nros_log::Logger)` unconditionally (`packages/api/nros-c/src/log.rs`), checking only for NULL.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG, THEN UB — the wrong pointer is dereferenced as a `Logger` and its name and level are read out of whatever bytes are there. NULL is the only value handled, and it is also what `nros_node_get_logger` returns for an uninitialised node, so the two failure modes are indistinguishable at the call site.

RFC-0089 says a refusal fires at the earliest point the defect is KNOWABLE, and for a pointer type that point is the TYPE: an opaque `struct nros_logger_s *` would make the mistake a compile error and costs nothing at runtime. The `extension` verdict above is unchanged — rcutils logging is declined as a whole — but the opaque-handle shape is the disposition this item should carry once the family is decided. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN on this row. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089), and the row's `extension` verdict rests on rcutils logging being declined as a whole, so the handle type has no upstream counterpart to adopt or refuse. The opaque-struct shape argued above is the fix for the CONVERSION hazard, not a disposition, and the family's own disposition belongs to whatever settles the rcutils decline.

c:logging_configure.why: rcl builds the logging system from `rcl_arguments_t*` (parsed argv) plus an `rcl_allocator_t`. Both constraints bite: an embedded image has no argv -- `rcl/arguments.h` is already excluded as plumbing for exactly that reason, and RFC-0045 bakes boot config instead -- and there is no allocator. Ours is `nros_log_init()` (C) / `nros_log::init(&'static [&'static dyn LogSink])` (Rust): a `'static` sink list, no arguments, no allocation. Records raised before it runs are not lost -- `nros_log::early` holds them in a fixed ring and `init` drains them into whatever sinks the board chose.

c:logging_configure_with_output_handler.why:
rcl's one-call form: configure the logging system from `rcl_arguments_t *` + an allocator AND install an output handler at the same time. Declined for the same reason as `c:logging_configure` — no argv and no allocator (RFC-0045) — so there is no arguments-taking configure for a handler-taking variant to extend.

CORRECTION (2026-09-13). This row was a `gap` whose whole stated reason was "see `c:logging_output_handler_t` -- a C caller cannot install a sink at all, so there is no handler-taking variant to have." A C caller CAN install a sink since phase-417 W4.d. What remains is only that we split the two calls rcl fuses: `nros_log_init()` then `nros_log_add_sink(sink, user_data)`, and the sink list is otherwise `'static` and board-chosen.

c:logging_fini.why: rcl tears the logging system down at shutdown. `nros_log` has no teardown by construction: `init` publishes the sink list into an `AtomicPtr` read lock-free on every dispatch and deliberately LEAKS the previous pointer, because a lock-free reader means nothing can prove when the old list stopped being read (`packages/core/nros-log/src/lib.rs`). What a user loses: no way to uninstall sinks. `nros_log::flush()` is the only lifecycle verb, and it is Rust-only -- `<nros/log.h>` declares no `nros_log_flush`, which is a small C gap of its own even though rcl has no `rcl_logging_flush` to name it here.

c:logging_multiple_output_handler.why: rcl's built-in handler that fans one record out to console + file + `/rosout`. Fan-out is our DEFAULT shape rather than a special handler -- `nros_log::init` takes a SLICE and `dispatch_to_sinks` walks all of it -- so there is no `multiple` variant to have. What a user loses is the destinations, not the fan-out: we ship no file sink (see `cpp:get_logging_directory`) and no `/rosout` sink (see `c:logging_rosout_enabled`), so the shipped list is one `PlatformSink` plus the optional `LogCrateSink`.

c:logging_output_handler_t.why:
rcl's installable log handler. We ship one; the SIGNATURE differs, and the constraint that makes it differ is the FFI mirror rule.

OURS: `nros_log_sink_fn` + `nros_log_add_sink(sink, user_data)` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/log.h`, phase-417 W4.d). It APPENDS, so a consumer teeing records to its own transport does not discard whatever the board installed, and records raised before any sink existed are replayed into the first one installed.

THE DIVERGENCE: rcl's handler takes a `rcutils_log_location_t *` STRUCT (file / function / line) plus a timestamp. Ours takes the same information as FLAT ARGUMENTS — `(user_data, severity, logger_name, logger_name_len, message, message_len, file, file_len, line, timestamp_ns)` — because cbindgen skips the logging module, so a struct crossing this FFI would be HAND-MIRRORED, and a mirror that misses an appended field passes a SHORTER struct than the reader reads. That is issue 0160's class, which has bitten three times. With flat arguments an appended field changes this TYPE, so every sink fails to COMPILE instead of reading stack garbage. Name and message are pointer+length rather than NUL-terminated for the reason `c:logger_get_name` states: the Rust side holds a length-delimited `&str`.

CORRECTION (2026-09-13). This was a `gap` asserting two things, both now false. (1) "a C or C++ caller cannot install a sink and must instead implement the `nros_platform_log_write` ABI in a board crate" — `nros_log_add_sink` landed in W4.d. (2) "the C emit path hardcodes `file: \"<nros-c>\", line: 0, timestamp_ns: 0`, so every record from a C or C++ call site reaches the sink with no location and no time" — `nros_log_emit_at` / `nros_log_emit_fmt_at` carry file and line, and the timestamp comes from `nros_log`'s own `__timestamp_ns()`, so C records are stamped by the same clock as Rust's (`packages/api/nros-c/src/log.rs`); `<nros-c>` survives only as the value for a caller that passes no file.

c:logging_rosout_enabled.why:
whether records are republished on the `/rosout` topic. We publish nothing there: `book/src/user-guide/logging.md:213` calls `/rosout` "explicitly out of scope today" and leaves room for an add-later `RosoutSink` alongside `PlatformSink`. This is a gap and not a divergence -- a `RosoutSink` is one publisher of `rcl_interfaces/msg/Log`, which static entity storage can hold, and the sink list is already the right shape for it (`packages/core/nros-log/README.md:27`). What a user loses is the standard way an operator reads logs off a running robot: `ros2 topic echo /rosout`, `rqt_console`, and every launch-side log aggregator see nothing from a nano-ros node. Note `nros-cpp`'s `rclcpp::NodeOptions::enable_rosout` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/options.hpp:256`) is REFUSE-LOUD — a dependent `static_assert` carrying `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_NODE_OPTIONS` — so a ported node that asks for rosout fails to compile naming the constraint; until phase-417 W3 it was a stored-and-ignored bool in the since-deleted `rclcpp_compat.hpp`, and got no diagnostic. Phase 379 W3.

VERDICT (phase-417 gap-verdict pass, 2026-09-21) — ABSENT. ABSENT AND NOT ADOPT, although a one-line `return false` would be a TRUE answer, because the row names the reason itself: `enable_rosout` is already REFUSE-LOUD, so a ported node that asks for rosout fails to COMPILE naming the constraint. That is the reach point. This predicate is reached only through the capability that refusal fires on, and RFC-0089 states the rule once — a member reached only through a refused type is absent, because diagnosing it twice teaches nothing and puts a message where no call site exists. If `/rosout` is ever built, this row becomes `adopt` on the same day and not before.

RE-READ (phase-444 gap re-read, 2026-09-23) — KEPT, re-measured and unchanged: `git grep RosoutSink -- packages` finds only `nros-log/README.md`'s "a future `RosoutSink`", there is no `/rosout` publisher, and the refusal is where the row says (the line moved 250 -> 256 and is corrected above). ONE THING TO FLAG RATHER THAN FIX HERE: the `/rosout` family does not agree with itself about what kind of difference this is. `cpp:RosoutQoS` (qos.json) records the same fact — "nano-ros publishes no `/rosout`" — as a DECLINE that STANDS, and `cpp:NodeOptions::rosout_qos` is `declined` too, while this row and the phase-417 roadmap say it becomes `adopt` the day a `RosoutSink` exists. Those are opposite claims about whether anybody decided. `gap` is kept here because the book's word is "today" and the sink list was SHAPED for the sink nobody has written; settling the family one way is a qos.json edit and belongs with whoever owns that shard. FAMILY SETTLED (phase-467 Q4, 2026-09-25) -- THIS ROW WAS THE ONE THE FAMILY AGREES WITH, and it is unchanged. `gap`+`absent` stands. The three `qos.json` siblings recorded the same `/rosout` absence as a DECLINE; two of them (`cpp:RosoutQoS`, `cpp:RosoutQoS::RosoutQoS`) have moved to `divergence`+`adopt-bounded`, because what they actually record is that the QoS profile TYPE ships while no runtime topic uses it. The topic is owed, and this is the row that owes it: a `RosoutSink` is one publisher of `rcl_interfaces/msg/Log` that static entity storage can hold, and the sink list is already the right shape for one.

c:node_get_logger.why:
rclc wraps none of rcutils logging, so a node-keyed logger accessor is ours over rclc; rclcpp's counterpart is `Node::get_logger()`, which our C++ does have (it correlates as `same`). Returns an opaque `const void*` = `&'static nros_log::Logger`, interned on the NODE'S OWN NAME (`packages/api/nros-c/src/node.rs` reads `node.name` and calls `nros_log::get_logger(name)`). Recorded here because it makes the node stage's `c:node_get_logger_name` row wrong on its facts: that row declined `rcl_node_get_logger_name` on the grounds that "nros_log takes an explicit logger name at the call site, so there is no derived name to fetch", and this function derives exactly that name -- `nros_log::Logger::name()` on the returned handle IS the answer, one C accessor away. W3/W5 should re-read `c:node_get_logger_name` as a gap.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-20, and it CORRECTS this row on its central fact.

THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS WRONG. This handle is NOT "interned on the NODE'S OWN NAME". `nros_node_get_logger` (`packages/api/nros-c/src/node.rs:679`) reads `node.name` and calls `nros_log::get_logger(name)`, and `get_logger` (`packages/core/nros-log/src/lib.rs:382`) is `INTERN.lookup(name).unwrap_or(&DEFAULT_LOGGER)` — LOOKUP ONLY. Interning is what `get_or_create_logger` does. So unless that exact name was interned earlier, every C node shares `DEFAULT_LOGGER`, whose name is the catch-all `"nros"`.

The follow-on inference is wrong too, and `c:node_get_logger_name` has been corrected: `Logger::name()` on the returned handle answers `"nros"` for every node, so it is not the derived name `rcl_node_get_logger_name` returns, and re-reading that row as a gap on THIS basis is unsound.

The recorded finding's other half — "C has no registration entry point" — is ALSO false: phase-417 W4.d added `nros_log_get_logger(const char *name)` (`packages/api/nros-c/src/log.rs:224`, declared in `packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/log.h`), which calls `get_or_create_logger` and DOES create. The entry point exists; nothing wires it to node init.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp::Node::get_logger()` returns a logger named for the node, so `RCLCPP_INFO(node->get_logger(), ...)` is per-node filterable.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG. Records carry logger name `"nros"`, and `nros_logger_set_level(nros_node_get_logger(&node), ...)` moves the threshold of EVERY node in the image — the exact aliasing `get_or_create_logger`'s own doc says it exists to prevent. Rust's `NodeHandle::logger()` (`packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/node.rs:145`) has the identical shape and says so honestly in its doc; the C accessor does not. Nothing platform-shaped forces the lookup — the creating call is one line away — so the disposition is ADOPT. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

DISPOSITION ADOPT, recorded in the field: `rclcpp::Node::get_logger()` returns a logger named for the node, the creating call (`nros_log::get_or_create_logger`) already exists and is one line from the accessor, and no platform constraint chooses lookup over create.

cpp:Logger.why:
rclcpp's `Logger` is a VALUE type holding a `std::string name_`, copied into every macro call, and `get_child` mints a new one by concatenating `parent.child`. Constraints: no allocator, and no `<string>` on a freestanding C++ build -- `nros-cpp` headers are compiled `-nostdinc++` against Zephyr's minimal libcpp, where the rule (RFC-0018, issue 0112) is to gate a std include on `NROS_CPP_STD` rather than `__STDC_HOSTED__`, because a hosted compiler invoked `-nostdinc++` still reports itself hosted. (`log.hpp` itself still gates its `<cstdio>` on `defined(NROS_CPP_STD) || (__STDC_HOSTED__ + 0)`; that one is the include 0112 explicitly left on the hosted gate, since minimal libcpp does provide `<cstdio>`.) Ours is an OPAQUE `const void*` returned by `Node::get_logger()` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/node.hpp`), pointing at a `&'static nros_log::Logger` in a bounded 32-slot intern table keyed on `&'static str`. `Logger::Logger` and `Logger::get_child` follow from that: a `void*` has no constructor and no allocator to build a child name with. What does NOT follow is that the accessors are missing -- see `cpp:Logger::get_name` and `cpp:Logger::set_level`. A named `nros::Logger` wrapper over the same handle would cost one struct and restore the type without restoring the allocation.

phase-428 W6 (2026-09-06) — disposition, required because this row's SHAPE CORRESPONDS: the name exists on the ported surface and the correlator files it `same`, so nothing in a build says the contract differs. That is the class RFC-0089 exists for.

FIRST, A CORRECTION to the text above, which says ours is "an OPAQUE `const void*` returned by `Node::get_logger()`". That is no longer the C++ surface. `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/log.hpp:246` declares a real `class rclcpp::Logger` holding a `const char* name_`, with `explicit Logger(const char* name = "")` and `get_name()`, alongside `rclcpp::get_logger(const char*)` and a `std::string` overload guarded by `NROS_CPP_HAS_STD_STRING`. The `const void*` is still the C spelling (`c:node_get_logger`); the C++ one moved in RFC-0089 stage 6 step A. The allocator argument above still explains why there is no `std::string` member and no `get_child`.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: the logger NAME reaches the output and keys per-logger level configuration; `get_child` mints a sub-logger by concatenation.

OURS: the name is carried and readable via `get_name()`, but the `RCLCPP_*` macros expand to `NROS_*`, which take no logger — the header says so in as many words: "The logger NAME is lost (nros has no per-logger dispatch yet)".

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: `logger.get_child("x")` is a COMPILE ERROR — no such member. The LOST NAME is not loud: a ported `RCLCPP_INFO(rclcpp::get_logger("planner"), ...)` compiles, logs, and attributes the line to nothing. That is the envelope, and it is stated in the header and not only here, which is what ADOPT-BOUNDED requires. `cpp:RCLCPP_FATAL` is the same discard measured on the severity rather than on the name.

cpp:Logger::set_level.why:
phase-417 W4.d (2026-09-13) — LANDED. This row read "see `c:log_levels_add_logger_setting` -- same missing accessor, C++ side. A ported node can raise or lower a logger in rclcpp and cannot here." It can now: `rclcpp::Logger::set_level(Level)` in `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/log.hpp`, a forwarder onto `nros_logger_set_level` (`<nros/log.h>`) onto `nros_log::Logger::set_level`. No level table and no comparison against one lives on the C++ side — RFC-0019 makes the Rust API the implementation, and a second threshold store is the defect this campaign has removed three times.

WHAT IS STILL BOUNDED, and it is two things.

(1) THE RETURN TYPE. Upstream's is `void` and it throws; RFC-0018 forbids exceptions, so a call that can fail says so in its return type. Same widening as `cpp:Executor::cancel`, and loud for the same reason: `nros::Result` carries `NROS_NODISCARD`, so a ported `logger.set_level(x);` written as a statement warns, and the `-D warnings` lanes make that an error.

(2) WHEN IT FAILS. A `Logger` built from a name alone (`rclcpp::Logger("planner")`, the one-argument constructor) or from an uninitialised node carries a NULL handle, and a threshold write through one is REFUSED rather than redirected. `detail::log_handle` does redirect a null handle to the catch-all and is right to — a RECORD with no owner belongs there — but a THRESHOLD WRITE with no owner does not: redirecting it would move the level of every unnamed logger in the image while reading, at the call site, as if it had moved "planner"'s. That is issue 1019's third defect pointing the other way. `rclcpp::get_logger("planner")` resolves the name and is not affected.

`Level` is upstream's nested enum and its values ARE `nros_log_severity_t`'s, which are rcutils's since phase-417 stage 3 (issue 1330), so the cast is an identity and there is no second number line to drift. It carries one value upstream has no counterpart for, `Trace` — `nros_log` has the level, and a `Level` that could not name it would leave C++ unable to reach a threshold C and Rust both reach.

HELD BY: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/logger_names_and_levels_runtime.cpp`, a COMPILE+LINK+RUN TU on the `just check cpp` lane. It measures the level through an INSTALLED SINK rather than through the getter, because a `set_level`/`get_level` pair over one shared cell would agree with itself and still drop the wrong records. Negative control, measured against a `set_level` that redirects a null handle to the catch-all: 2 failures.

cpp:Node::get_logger.why:
phase-428 W6 remainder (2026-09-06) — ledgered because the correlator's return-type comparison became a VERDICT. `rclcpp::Node::get_logger()` returns `rclcpp::Logger` BY VALUE — a real object carrying the node's fully-qualified name, which is what makes `RCLCPP_INFO(this->get_logger(), ...)` print under the node's own name. Ours returns `rclcpp::Logger` too — `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/node.hpp` builds one from the node's name and the handle `nros_cpp_node_get_logger` answers.

CORRECTION (2026-09-13): this row said ours returns `const void*`. That was true when it was written and stopped being true at phase-427 W5, which merged the two colliding `get_logger()` spellings onto upstream's return type; the row is the record of a return-type comparison, so the one fact it is FOR had gone stale. What remains is that the TYPE is still opaque inside — see (1) below — which is what keeps the disposition at adopt-bounded. Two things follow, and the second corrects this campaign's own record.

(1) The TYPE is opaque by construction: RFC-0054 makes the C header the ABI SSoT, and a logger handle crossing that boundary is a pointer. A ported file that passes the result to a logging macro is unaffected, and so is one that names `rclcpp::Logger` explicitly or calls `.get_name()` or `.set_level()` on it — both exist (the latter since phase-417 W4.d, `cpp:Logger::set_level`). `get_child()` is the one that still does not compile, and has its own row. That is the bound, and it is why this is `adopt-bounded`.

(2) phase-428 W5's CORRECTION section already established that BOTH the C++ and the Rust paths fall back to a sentinel/`DEFAULT_LOGGER`, so the asymmetry argument in RFC-0089 §"get_logger follows ROS 2" does not hold. This row does NOT reopen that; it records only what the two return types are, which is the question the gate asks. The per-node logger identity is tracked where W5 left it.

c:log_severity_t.why:
WHAT IS STILL OWED, and after phase-467 it is ONLY THE ANCESTRY. rcutils resolves a logger with no level of its own by walking the dotted ancestry its name spells (`x.y.z` → `x.y` → `x`, `rcutils_logging_get_logger_effective_level`) and only then falling to `g_rcutils_logging_default_logger_level`. `nros_log` walks nothing and falls straight to that last step. `adopt-bounded` is that bound, and the bound is behaviourally complete here: `get_logger` is exact string equality over `MAX_LOGGERS` = 32 slots (`packages/core/nros-log/src/lib.rs`, `InternTable::lookup`), no logger name in the tree is dotted, and a walk over a linear 32-slot table is a cost with no consumer. Building it is a `nros-log` change, not a C-API one.

LANDED phase-467 — `UNSET` MEANS INHERIT NOW, which is what every previous version of this row recorded as owed. `nros_logger_set_level(logger, NROS_LOG_SEVERITY_UNSET)` takes that logger's own level AWAY instead of banding down to `TRACE`, and the logger then filters on one process-wide default: `nros_log_set_default_level` / `nros_log_get_default_level` in C, `nros_log::Logger::set_default_level` / `::default_level` in Rust — the same byte, which is why this row and `rust:Logger::set_default_level` were one mechanism and are closed together. A logger that STATES a level is not overridden: `Logger::new` now stores a sentinel that is distinct from `with_level(.., Info)`, because "the author did not choose" and "the author chose Info" are different statements and one default cannot move both. The sentinel is `u8::MAX`, NOT `0` — `Severity::Trace = 0`, which is exactly why storing rcutils's `UNSET` in a level byte used to select the most verbose level — and being above `Fatal` rather than below `Trace` means an unresolved sentinel can only ever suppress a record, never emit one.

UNSET IS SPECIAL ONLY WHERE A LEVEL IS STORED. Passed as a record's severity or as a threshold question (`nros_log_emit`, `nros_logger_is_enabled`) `0` still bands to `TRACE`: "no level set" is not a level to emit at, `rcutils_logging_logger_is_enabled_for` just compares the number too, and making one of these entry points reject a value the others must accept would cost the totality the transparent newtype exists to give. The one inversion is the DEFAULT itself: `nros_log_set_default_level(UNSET)` restores `INFO`, because the default has nothing to inherit from — `rcutils_logging_set_default_logger_level` documents exactly that, and `RCUTILS_DEFAULT_LOGGER_DEFAULT_LEVEL` is `RCUTILS_LOG_SEVERITY_INFO` (`rcutils/logging.h:43`).

THE HOT PATH IS MEASURED, not reasoned about. `Logger::is_enabled` is every log macro's first act on every target, so resolving the sentinel SELECTS the byte to compare against and compares once, rather than comparing twice and short-circuiting. At an inlined call site with `rustc -O`: `thumbv7m-none-eabi` 8 instructions before, 13 after and still BRANCH-FREE (LLVM predicates the whole fallback into one `ittt eq` block), against 16 with a branch for the short-circuit form; `x86_64` 4 before, 10 after with one branch on the logger's own byte, against 12. The cost over the original is one compare against an immediate, plus a byte load of one process-global that a logger with its own level never performs.

UPSTREAM'S DOC BLOCK DOES NOT PROMISE ANY OF THIS, AND THIS ROW USED TO CITE IT AS IF IT DID. The whole behavioural text of `rcutils_logging_set_logger_level` in `/opt/ros/humble/include/rcutils/rcutils/logging.h` (read IN THE `ros2` box — the host is Arch and has no `/opt/ros` at all) is: "If an empty string is specified as the name, the `g_rcutils_logging_default_logger_level` will be set." Nothing about `UNSET` as a VALUE. The "UNSET restores the default" sentence belongs to `set_default_logger_level` and "returns UNSET if unset" to `get_logger_leveln` — two other functions. So the claim was an inference from three places, shipped to users as a flat assertion, in our header and in `to_facade`'s doc.

MEASURED INSTEAD, against the implementation the box actually links. `rcutils/src/logging.c` is not on this machine (`/opt/ros/humble` ships headers and libs; `/opt/ros/humble/src` holds only gmock/gtest) and `apt-get source` needs a `deb-src` line, i.e. `sudo` — so it was fetched from `ros2/rcutils` at TAG `5.1.9`, the version `dpkg -s ros-humble-rcutils` reports, whose `include/rcutils/logging.h` is MD5-IDENTICAL to the installed header (`a90cb816…`); that identity is what makes the tag the right source rather than a guess, and the `humble` branch head happens to be byte-identical too. There: `set_logger_level(name, UNSET)` is NOT rejected and does NOT erase the entry — it stores the STRING `"UNSET"` (`g_rcutils_log_severity_names[0]`) in the severity map; `get_logger_leveln` maps it back to `RCUTILS_LOG_SEVERITY_UNSET`; and `get_logger_effective_level` treats that exactly as it treats an absent entry, continuing the walk and falling to the default. The behaviour we adopted is real. The GUARANTEE is not, and both call sites now say which of the two they cite.

LANDED, and this half is history — kept because it is the numbering a reader needs. The C `enum` is on rcutils's number line (`UNSET=0, DEBUG=10, INFO=20, WARN=30, ERROR=40, FATAL=50`), so a ported rcutils-numbered constant, a value read from a config file and an integer from the environment all mean here what they mean upstream. Our `TRACE` (rcutils has none) takes `5`, inside rcutils's own `UNSET`..`DEBUG` gap. The Rust mirror is `#[repr(transparent)]` over `c_int` instead of `#[repr(u8)]`, which removes the width mismatch and the UB outright: no integer is an invalid discriminant, and `to_facade` is TOTAL, resolving by BAND so a threshold written between two named levels lands on the named level at or below it. `<nros/log.h>` carries the width and two value `static_assert`s (the hand-mirrored-FFI class one layer over from `check-ffi-struct-mirrors`); `log::severity_tests` carries the numbering, the banding, the round-trip and the every-integer-resolves property.

RE-READ (phase-444 gap re-read, 2026-09-23) — KEPT `gap`, now for the ancestry alone. **This row is also the worked example for issue 1463**: `stale_gaps()` exempts every `gap` that carries a disposition, so a row whose first paragraphs said LANDED and FIXED sat in the campaign's work queue for twelve days with nothing able to ask. The exemption is right for a behaviour defect on a shared name — which is what the first paragraph above still is — but its REACH is every dispositioned gap, which is wider than the rule it implements.

phase-467 (2026-09-25) — RE-VERDICTED `gap` → `divergence`, disposition unchanged at `adopt-bounded`. The remaining debt was the ancestry alone, and measured, the ancestry is PERMANENT here rather than merely unbuilt — which is a different sentence and belongs under a different verdict, because `gap` means "we should too, nobody has done it" and that is now the wrong claim. The constraint is RFC-0036-shaped (no allocator), reached in three steps:

1. THE HIERARCHY HAS NO PRODUCER, AND THE PRODUCER IS ITSELF A DIVERGENCE ON THAT CONSTRAINT. Upstream's dotted names come from `Logger::get_child` / `Logger::create_child` — the separator is a published constant, `RCUTILS_LOGGING_SEPARATOR_STRING "."` (rcutils 5.1.9 `rcutils/logging.h`, read in the `ros2` box). Both are already `divergence` rows in THIS shard (`rust:Logger::create_child`, `cpp:Logger::get_child`) and each names the same constraint: there is no allocator to concatenate `parent.child` at run time and the intern table holds `&'static str`. So the walk's only intended producer is refused one layer up, and an ancestry resolver built here would resolve a hierarchy nothing can construct.

2. UPSTREAM'S RESOLVER READS A STRUCTURE WE DO NOT HAVE, AND "NO ALLOCATOR" IS AGAIN WHY. rcutils keys a level by NAME, not by logger: `rcutils_logging_set_logger_level(const char *name, int level)` writes an allocator-backed severity MAP — the header names it in its own error code, `RCUTILS_RET_LOGGING_SEVERITY_MAP_INVALID` — so an ANCESTOR can carry a level without being a logger at all, which is the entire point of the walk. Ours keys the level by OBJECT: `nros_logger_set_level(logger, level)` takes a HANDLE and the level is an `AtomicU8` inside the `Logger`. Giving an ancestor a level here therefore means MATERIALISING it — one of `MAX_LOGGERS` = 32 intern slots plus name-arena bytes spent on an entity that emits no records. The loop is not the expensive half; the name-keyed map it reads is.

3. AND IT WOULD BE PAID ON THE HOT PATH, PER RECORD. `Logger::is_enabled` is every log macro's first act on every target. The ONE-step fallback this phase landed measured 8 → 13 instructions inlined on `thumbv7m-none-eabi`, still branch-free. A walk is a loop over `.`-separated prefixes with a 32-slot LINEAR scan per step — O(depth × 32) string compares where there is now one compare against an immediate.

WHAT A USER LOSES, stated exactly, because `adopt-bounded` means the envelope is part of the API. A dotted name is ACCEPTED and is simply one flat name: `nros_log_get_logger("nav.costmap")` interns a name that contains a dot, and setting `nav`'s level does not move it, because `nav` here is a different logger and not an ancestor. A ported file that relied on prefix inheritance loses it, and finds out by a threshold not moving rather than by a diagnostic — which is why the envelope is STATED beside the enum in `packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/log.h` and on `nros_log`'s process default, not only here. Note the earlier wording "no logger name in the tree is dotted" was true and was the WRONG argument: it is a fact about today's names, and a user can write a dotted one whenever they like. The argument that holds is that a dot here buys no parent.

So this row stops being campaign work. If `create_child` ever lands — it needs the allocator or a name arena its own row does not have — this decision is re-openable, and the re-opening belongs to THAT row, not this one.

A forwarder, like every other member of this trio (RFC-0019). phase-467 — the process-wide default threshold, reachable from C. The byte itself lives in `nros_log` (RFC-0019: the Rust API is the implementation, C delegates); this is a pointer-free forwarder onto `nros_log::Logger::set_default_level` / `::default_level`.

EXTENSION, and the reason is the recorded surface rather than upstream's design: rcl's counterpart is `rcutils_logging_set_default_logger_level` / `..._get_default_logger_level`, which the recorded rclc surface does not carry, so there is no upstream row to correlate against — the same reason `c:logger_set_level` and `c:logger_get_level` are extensions. rust:Logger::unset_level.why:
phase-467 — take a logger's OWN level away, so it filters on `Logger::default_level()` again. rclrs HAS this capability and spells it `logger.set_level(LogSeverity::Unset)`; the C surface here spells it upstream's way too (`nros_logger_set_level(logger, NROS_LOG_SEVERITY_UNSET)`, row `c:log_severity_t`). Rust cannot, and the reason is the platform ABI.

`nros_log::Severity` is `#[repr(u8)]` and its discriminants ARE the `nros_platform_log_write` ABI — the number a board's sink receives and renders. Every value it can hold must therefore be a level something can EMIT AT, and `Unset` is not: it is a statement about a stored threshold. Adding the variant would put a value no sink can render into every `match` on a record's severity, into `severity_from_u8`, and into `is_enabled(Severity::Unset)`, where it means nothing. So the state gets a VERB instead of a value, and the one place a caller can mean it — writing a level — is the one place the verb exists.

The C mirror keeps upstream's spelling for the opposite reason, and the contrast is the point: `nros_log_severity_t` is a transparent newtype over `c_int` precisely because C's `enum` is unfixed and any `int` may arrive, so it is TOTAL and `0` costs it nothing. A Rust `enum` is not total, which is what makes the same value a liability on one side and free on the other.

rust:Logger::default_level.why:
phase-467 — read the process-wide default that `Logger::set_default_level` writes. rclrs has no counterpart: `rcutils_logging_get_default_logger_level` exists, but rclrs binds only the setter, so there is nothing in the recorded surface to correlate against — the same position `rust:Logger::level` is in one level down.

It is here because C needs it (`nros_log_get_default_level` forwards to it, and RFC-0019 keeps the store on the Rust side) and because a setter with no getter is the shape phase-417 W4.d spent a wave removing: `Logger::get_level` was added to C++ for exactly this reason, "the one language missing it was the thing to fix".
